changes: Build promotion now preserves an executable POSIX CLI and fails closed on package-manifest read errors; doctor verifies package/PATH agreement, bin-target containment, and actual Windows npm shim contents; regression fixtures cover worktree rebuilds, target escapes, missing PATH commands, zero-assertion skips, and safe PowerShell remediation.
usage: Run npm --prefix packages/main run build, then proof-or-stop --version and proof-or-stop doctor; a healthy installation reports contract: global-core-realpath-pass only after the host-specific executable contract is verified.
expectedOutcome: After rebuilding from the main checkout or a Story worktree, the globally linked proof-or-stop command remains runnable; doctor never reports a healthy global core when the selected command, target, permissions, or Windows shim disagree.
actualTranscript: Current-material focused tests passed: ok global-core-realpath and contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored, including the manifest-read fail-closed case. Full proof-or-stop validate executed all 132 configured commands and returned status=pass and allPass=true.
outcomeDiff: No difference: the observed focused and full-suite results match the expected cross-platform fail-closed behavior.
limitations: Real POSIX executable behavior was exercised on the current macOS host; Windows command-shim behavior and encoded PowerShell remediation were exercised through deterministic platform-injected fixtures rather than a physical Windows host.
pitfalls: The original EACCES came from build promotion replacing the globally linked dist target with mode 0644. Review then exposed related false-green paths in PATH selection, symlink containment, Windows shim checks, percent expansion, and swallowed manifest read errors; all were current acceptance blockers and were repaired. Full validation includes a quorum smoke that legitimately runs for about ten minutes with heartbeats. The unrelated unmatched --grep zero-check issue belongs to B-e40f and was not pulled into this Story.
